timeline_events.summary: WikiLeaks published more than 250,000 classified US embassy cables, revealing confidential diplomatic assessments of US allies and foes.
WikiLeaks unveils a graphic video of a 2007 US Army attack in Iraq that left 12 people dead, including two Reuters employees.
Chelsea Manning, the US army intelligence analyst who leaked a huge cache of state secrets to WikiLeaks, was arrested at Forward Operating Base Hammer outside Baghdad.
US officials are searching for WikiLeaks founder Julian Assange in an attempt to pressure him not to publish thousands of confidential diplomatic cables.
WikiLeaks says it plans to release a secret military video of a deadly US air strike on the Afghan village of Garani in May 2009.

WikiLeaks founder Julian Assange is profiled as the driving force behind the site, which has published over a million confidential documents and faced more than 100 legal attacks since its 2007 launch.
WikiLeaks obtains and discloses more than 90,000 secret US military records about the Afghanistan war, one of the biggest leaks in US military history.
The White House implores WikiLeaks to stop posting secret Afghanistan war documents, saying the logs jeopardize national security.

WikiLeaks founder Julian Assange revealed the organization is preparing to publish around 15,000 withheld Afghanistan war logs after finishing checks, prompting condemnation from Reporters Without Borders and anger from the Pentagon.

Michael Moore and Daniel Ellsberg launch an international campaign demanding the release of Bradley Manning, the US soldier charged with passing classified material to WikiLeaks, with demonstrations planned in the US, Canada, and Australia over the next three days.

WikiLeaks founder Julian Assange accused Wired magazine of having an agenda, not checking facts, and spreading misinformation about WikiLeaks, including a claim that the site was due to release as many as 500,000 classified US documents from the Iraq war.
US Secretary of State Hillary Clinton and NATO condemned WikiLeaks' release of almost 400,000 secret US army field reports from the Iraq war, claiming the disclosure could put lives at risk.
WikiLeaks releases a second large trove of leaked US military material, the Iraq war logs, escalating tensions with Washington.

WikiLeaks releases almost 400,000 secret US military field reports on the Iraq war, revealing previously undocumented civilian deaths and abuse, and Julian Assange speaks at a London press conference about the disclosure.

The UK Ministry of Defence released details of 21 incidents in which British troops attacked Afghan civilians, incidents that were among thousands mentioned in US army logs posted by WikiLeaks in the summer.
WikiLeaks released a trove of U.S. diplomatic cables, sparking debate over secrecy and media coverage.
WikiLeaks founder Julian Assange and his lawyer threatened to sue The Guardian over its plan to publish stories based on the US embassy cables, leading to a further delay in publication.
The UK government acknowledged it had been warned by US authorities about WikiLeaks’ expected publication of sensitive diplomatic files, with Washington braced for the release within days.

World leaders were briefed by the US state department about expected WikiLeaks disclosures of thousands of sensitive diplomatic cables, and newspaper editors were asked to brief the government if they plan to publish sensitive diplomatic files.
WikiLeaks released 251,287 secret US embassy cables, the largest leak of diplomatic missives in history, which were published by the Guardian and international partners.
The Guardian publishes the first in a series of reports based on more than 250,000 US embassy cables sent to WikiLeaks, with five publications having had prior access.

Interpol added WikiLeaks founder Julian Assange to its worldwide wanted list on sex-crime allegations, as the US announced an active criminal investigation into whether he violated its espionage laws.
WikiLeaks founder Julian Assange is scheduled to answer Guardian readers' questions live online at 1 pm, subject to his access to an internet connection.

The Guardian published a series of stories sourced from US embassy cables via WikiLeaks, revealing allegations including organized crime linked to the Russian government, China's growing impatience with North Korea, and alleged corruption in the Afghan government.

Tableau Software removed its visualizations of the leaked US embassy cables from the internet after a public request from Senator Joe Lieberman, who called for organizations hosting WikiLeaks to terminate their relationship with the website.

WikiLeaks founder Julian Assange agreed to meet British police regarding a European arrest warrant from Sweden, while US Attorney General Eric Holder authorized significant actions toward prosecuting him over the release of diplomatic cables.
WikiLeaks founder Julian Assange is expected to appear in a UK court after his lawyers said he would meet police regarding a European arrest warrant from Sweden over alleged sexual assaults.
WikiLeaks says it will continue releasing leaked US embassy cables despite the arrest of founder Julian Assange in London on Swedish sexual offence allegations.
WikiLeaks founder Julian Assange is denied bail by a UK court due to his lack of community ties in the UK.
WikiLeaks founder Julian Assange was remanded in custody in London pending extradition proceedings over sexual offence allegations made in Sweden.
Lawyers for WikiLeaks editor-in-chief Julian Assange said they are preparing for a possible US indictment, though no charges have yet been lodged.
WikiLeaks founder Julian Assange, speaking from his Wandsworth prison cell, urges supporters to protect WikiLeaks from "instruments of US foreign policy."
The Crown Prosecution Service, not Swedish prosecutors, made the decision to oppose bail for WikiLeaks founder Julian Assange, who remains in Wandsworth prison.
Britain's high court granted bail to WikiLeaks founder Julian Assange, who is wanted in Sweden for questioning over allegations of rape.
Julian Assange said his life and the lives of his WikiLeaks colleagues are under threat, and Bank of America became the latest financial institution to refuse to handle payments for WikiLeaks.

The Belarus-Telegraf state newspaper says WikiLeaks allowed the Belarusian dictatorship to identify organizers, instigators and rioters, including foreign ones, who protested against rigged elections.
The CIA launches a taskforce named the WikiLeaks Task Force (WTF) to assess the impact of 250,000 leaked US diplomatic cables.
The US State Department relocated a handful of foreign diplomatic sources identified in secret embassy cables released via WikiLeaks and warned hundreds of others about their safety.
Julian Assange appeared in court for a procedural hearing on his extradition to Sweden and said WikiLeaks would continue its work unabated.

Senior US State Department officials concluded in private briefings to Congress that the WikiLeaks controversy has caused little real and lasting damage to American diplomacy, contradicting the White House's public condemnation.
A Guardian book reveals that WikiLeaks founder Julian Assange disguised himself as an old woman in a wig for fear he was being followed by US intelligence.
WikiLeaks founder Julian Assange appears in court for a two-day hearing to resist extradition to Sweden.
Julian Assange's lawyer made a graphic defence during an extradition hearing at Belmarsh magistrate's court in London, denying sexual assault allegations against the WikiLeaks founder.

The Australian ambassador to Sweden wrote to Sweden’s justice minister seeking assurances that WikiLeaks founder Julian Assange would be treated justly under Swedish and international law if extradited there.

WikiLeaks founder Julian Assange lost his extradition battle at Belmarsh magistrates court and is to be extradited to Sweden to face allegations of rape and sexual assault, though his legal team confirmed he will appeal.
Lawyers for WikiLeaks founder Julian Assange lodged papers to appeal his extradition from Britain to Sweden to face allegations of rape and sexual assault.
The Hindu newspaper began publishing reports based on US diplomatic cables obtained from WikiLeaks, covering Washington's relationship with New Delhi.
The Guardian was named newspaper of the year at the 2011 Press Awards for its partnership with WikiLeaks on the leaked US embassy cables.

A leading British MP warned that President Barack Obama may have prejudiced the trial of US army private Bradley Manning, who is charged with leaking classified US documents to WikiLeaks, by saying at a fundraiser that Manning "broke the law".
WikiLeaks founder Julian Assange appeared at the high court in London at the start of his latest fight against extradition to Sweden over sex allegations.

A security breach led to the unredacted WikiLeaks archive of 251,000 secret US diplomatic cables being made available online, with WikiLeaks blaming the Guardian's book for the release and the Guardian denying the allegations.
WikiLeaks published its full archive of 251,000 unredacted US diplomatic cables, potentially exposing named individuals to detention or harm, a move condemned by its five previous media partners.

The Iraqi government announces a new investigation into a 2006 massacre of a family in Ishaqi after WikiLeaks released a diplomatic cable alleging US soldiers handcuffed and executed women and children and called in an air strike to destroy evidence.
WikiLeaks announced it will suspend operations until the banking blockade by Visa, Mastercard, and PayPal is lifted, warning it lacks funds to continue into 2012 at current funding levels.
The high court dismissed Julian Assange's appeal against extradition to Sweden, narrowing the WikiLeaks founder's legal options.
WikiLeaks founder Julian Assange seeks to take his extradition fight to the UK supreme court by applying for a hearing to appeal against extradition to Sweden over sex crime allegations.

Two judges ruled that Julian Assange, founder of WikiLeaks, could petition the UK supreme court for permission to appeal against his extradition to Sweden, delaying his otherwise imminent extradition.
A panel of seven UK supreme court justices is to hear Julian Assange's appeal against extradition to Sweden, with a two-day hearing scheduled to begin on 1 February.
A forensic investigator testified that files on Bradley Manning's army computers exactly matched WikiLeaks-published US embassy cables and Guantánamo detainee reports.

US army prosecutors allege they found email correspondence between Bradley Manning and WikiLeaks founder Julian Assange in which Manning expressed hope that publishing classified Iraq and Afghanistan war reports would remove the fog of war.
WikiLeaks begins releasing a cache of what it says are 5.5 million emails obtained from the servers of the US-based intelligence gathering firm Stratfor, initially publishing 167 emails.
A book chapter argues that mainstream media coverage of WikiLeaks' US diplomatic cables marginalized stories of significant public interest and delegitimized WikiLeaks.

The military judge in Bradley Manning's court-martial refused to dismiss the most serious charge of aiding the enemy but warned prosecutors they must prove Manning knew he was helping the enemy by allegedly handing hundreds of thousands of secret US documents to WikiLeaks.
Bradley Manning marks two years of imprisonment in a military prison for allegedly leaking the 2007 "Collateral Murder" video and other documents to WikiLeaks.
Bradley Manning's lawyer files a motion stating the US government possesses 250,000 pages of documents relating to WikiLeaks and Manning but is refusing to disclose them to the defense.

Bradley Manning's lawyer accuses US military prosecutors of misleading the court and withholding evidence about the damage caused by WikiLeaks disclosures, alleging the government is deliberately preventing a fair trial.
WikiLeaks founder Julian Assange seeks political asylum at the Ecuadorean embassy in London, sparking a legal crisis over his extradition case.
WikiLeaks founder Julian Assange sought political asylum at the Ecuadorean embassy in London after the UK Supreme Court rejected his appeal against extradition to Sweden.
Julian Assange seeks asylum at Ecuador’s London embassy, with his lawyer stating concern that Sweden might extradite him to the United States over WikiLeaks.

A military judge ordered prosecutors to prepare a due diligence statement and hand over damage assessments related to WikiLeaks' publication of secret diplomatic cables and war logs in the Bradley Manning case.

WikiLeaks founder Julian Assange refuses to comply with a Metropolitan Police request to surrender himself to a London police station, remaining in the Ecuadorean embassy while seeking political asylum.
The US Department of Justice confirms that WikiLeaks remains the object of an ongoing criminal investigation.
Baltasar Garzón will lead the legal team representing Julian Assange and WikiLeaks.

Ecuador’s foreign minister says Britain told Ecuador it believes officials can enter its London embassy and arrest WikiLeaks founder Julian Assange, and Ecuador says it will announce its decision on Assange’s asylum request on Thursday.
Ecuadorian officials say President Rafael Correa has agreed to grant WikiLeaks founder Julian Assange asylum, though Correa denies a decision has been made.
Ecuador remains willing to negotiate with Britain over Julian Assange’s fate and proposes that the UK and Sweden undertake not to extradite him to a third country after the Swedish investigation.

Ecuador's foreign minister says Ecuador received a written threat from the UK that it could arrest WikiLeaks founder Julian Assange at Ecuador's embassy in London, and Ecuador is considering his asylum request.
Ecuador grants political asylum to WikiLeaks founder Julian Assange, prompting a diplomatic row with the UK and Sweden.

Ecuador's president warns the UK that entering its London embassy to seize WikiLeaks founder Julian Assange would be an act of political suicide, amid a standoff over Ecuador's decision to grant him political asylum.
A police officer accidentally revealed a document showing plans to arrest WikiLeaks founder Julian Assange "under all circumstances" if he leaves the Ecuadorean embassy in London.
A military judge set the court-martial trial of WikiLeaks suspect Bradley Manning for February 2013, with Manning facing 22 counts related to leaking secret US documents to WikiLeaks.
Ofcom did not uphold Julian Assange's complaint that a More4 documentary about WikiLeaks was unfair and violated his privacy.
WikiLeaks founder Julian Assange announces he will publish a new book, "Cypherpunks: Freedom and the Future of the Internet," on 26 November.

A pre-trial hearing in the court-martial of WikiLeaks suspect Bradley Manning concluded, with the judge yet to rule on whether Manning's nine months of pre-trial confinement should reduce his sentence.
Julian Assange said WikiLeaks is preparing to publish 1 million new secret government documents as he marked six months of refuge in the Ecuadorean embassy in London.
A military judge granted Bradley Manning a 112-day reduction in any eventual sentence for excessively harsh pre-trial detention in the WikiLeaks case, but declined to dismiss the charges.
A military judge delays Bradley Manning's trial until June in the WikiLeaks state secrets case, after granting him a 112-day sentence reduction for harsh pre-trial detention.
A former confidante of WikiLeaks suspect Bradley Manning defended her decision to hold an online Q&A about his forthcoming trial despite being named as a key defence witness.
A judge ruled that Bradley Manning, accused of leaking state secrets to WikiLeaks, will largely be barred from presenting evidence about his motives in his court martial.
Principal photography begins on The Fifth Estate, a film about WikiLeaks founder Julian Assange, with Benedict Cumberbatch in the lead role.
A documentary about WikiLeaks, We Steal Secrets: The Story of WikiLeaks, premiered at the Sundance Film Festival.

Julian Assange, speaking via videolink from the Ecuadorian embassy, attacks the upcoming WikiLeaks movie "The Fifth Estate," calling it "a lie upon lie" and "a massive propaganda attack on WikiLeaks."

Bradley Manning is expected to plead guilty to lesser charges, including wilfully communicating classified documents to WikiLeaks, while pleading not guilty to major charges such as aiding the enemy at his court martial hearing.
Ecuadorean diplomats raise Julian Assange's case with the Labour party as part of attempts to resolve the diplomatic standoff over the WikiLeaks founder.

Icelandic MP Birgitta Jónsdóttir, part of the WikiLeaks team that produced the 2010 "Collateral Murder" video, arrives in the US to stage a New York exhibition of stills from the video marking its third anniversary and to protest the US government's clampdown on whistleblowers.
WikiLeaks publishes over 1.7 million US diplomatic and intelligence records from 1973 to 1976 in a searchable collection called the Public Library of US Diplomacy (PlusD).

WikiLeaks releases over 1.7 million US diplomatic cables from Henry Kissinger's tenure as secretary of state (1973-1976), documents already released by the US National Archives and Records Administration, which WikiLeaks has made more accessible by converting them into searchable formats.
Supporters of accused WikiLeaks source Bradley Manning rallied outside Fort Meade ahead of his court martial, which was set to open on 2013-06-03.
US prosecutors alleged in the Bradley Manning trial that Julian Assange and WikiLeaks had close ties with Manning, guiding his leaks and involving him in the editing process.
The trial of Bradley Manning, accused of leaking classified documents to WikiLeaks, opens at Fort Meade, Maryland, with legal experts warning it could set a dangerous precedent for free speech.
Ecuador's foreign minister Ricardo Patino plans to visit London to meet Julian Assange at the Ecuadorian embassy, on the eve of the first anniversary of Assange's stay there.

Ecuador's foreign minister says WikiLeaks founder Julian Assange is prepared to spend another five years in the Ecuadorean embassy in London, as British and Ecuadorean legal experts agree to try to resolve the impasse.
Julian Assange said he will not leave Ecuador’s embassy even if Sweden drops its extradition bid, citing fear of a sealed US indictment and prosecution over WikiLeaks cable releases.

Defence lawyers for Bradley Manning, who leaked state secrets to WikiLeaks, filed motions calling for several charges against him to be dismissed, including the most serious charge of "aiding the enemy."
The first trailer for The Fifth Estate, a film about WikiLeaks and Julian Assange, is released online.
The judge in Bradley Manning’s court martial declined to dismiss the “aiding the enemy” charge related to his leaking of state secrets posted by WikiLeaks.

In closing arguments at Bradley Manning’s court-martial, the prosecution accuses Manning of transmitting hundreds of thousands of classified documents to WikiLeaks for notoriety and argues WikiLeaks was not a journalistic organization.

The WikiLeaks party unveils its candidates and abridged policy platform for the upcoming Australian federal Senate election, with Julian Assange appearing via Skype from the Ecuadorian embassy in London.
Bradley Manning, the source of the WikiLeaks disclosures, was convicted on most charges including seven Espionage Act counts but acquitted of the most serious charge of "aiding the enemy."
A military judge reduced Bradley Manning's maximum possible sentence for leaking state secrets to WikiLeaks from 136 years to a possible 90 years by merging several counts.
US government requests that Bradley Manning, who leaked classified documents to WikiLeaks, be sentenced to 60 years in prison.
Chelsea Manning formally appeals to President Obama for a presidential pardon or commuted sentence for transmitting hundreds of thousands of state secrets to WikiLeaks.
Benedict Cumberbatch reveals Julian Assange sent him a 10-page email the day before filming began, urging him not to take part in The Fifth Estate, a film about WikiLeaks.

Ecuador's foreign minister accuses the British government of violating Julian Assange's human rights and says there is no UK will to find a diplomatic solution to his confinement in Ecuador's London embassy.
Chelsea Manning says the military is continuing to deny her gender-reassignment treatment a year after she was sentenced to 35 years in prison for giving secret documents to WikiLeaks.
Chelsea Manning, who was arrested for passing state secrets to WikiLeaks, breaks silence to criticize Obama's Isis strategy.
Chelsea Manning, who leaked secret documents to WikiLeaks, sues the US military over denial of gender dysphoria treatment.
Google revealed to WikiLeaks that it had handed over emails and other digital data belonging to three WikiLeaks staffers to the US government under a secret search warrant.
WikiLeaks released secret CIA files, including one on maintaining cover with fake IDs at foreign airports and a 2009 assessment of the CIA’s assassination program.

The Justice Department obtained a secret 2012 warrant to seize the contents and metadata of three WikiLeaks staffers' personal Gmail accounts, which was kept secret from them for almost two and a half years.
WikiLeaks demands answers after Google handed staff emails and digital data to the US government.
A federal judge confirms that the US government is conducting an ongoing, long-term criminal investigation into WikiLeaks.
Chelsea Manning, the US soldier imprisoned for leaking state secrets to WikiLeaks, joins Twitter with the handle @xychelsea, attracting over 1,000 followers before posting.

Chelsea Manning, serving 35 years in military prison for leaking state secrets to WikiLeaks, posted a handwritten letter on her new Twitter feed explaining that her tweets are dictated by phone to supporters, in a move to quash conspiracy theories claiming the feed is a fraud.
The French government rejects Julian Assange's asylum request, stating he is not in immediate danger.

Sweden offers to negotiate an agreement with Ecuador to allow Swedish prosecutors to interview WikiLeaks founder Julian Assange in the Ecuadorian embassy in London, though the statute of limitations on some allegations is about to expire.

Chelsea Manning was found guilty of possessing unapproved reading material by a Fort Leavenworth prison panel and sentenced to 21 days of recreational restrictions, avoiding solitary confinement; she was serving a 35-year sentence for leaking US state secrets to WikiLeaks.
Documents reportedly show Ecuadorian officials considered smuggling WikiLeaks editor-in-chief Julian Assange out of their London embassy in fancy dress or via other plots to evade police.

Scotland Yard calls off its 24-hour surveillance of the Ecuadorian embassy where WikiLeaks founder Julian Assange has been living, saying the operation is no longer proportionate, while stating that efforts to arrest him continue.

Ecuador requests that the UK grant WikiLeaks founder Julian Assange safe passage from its London embassy to a hospital for an MRI scan, which Britain declines while stating he can leave but faces arrest under a valid European arrest warrant.
The Metropolitan police confirmed that WikiLeaks founder Julian Assange would be arrested if he left the Ecuadorian embassy in London to go to hospital for a medical examination.
WikiLeaks released documents it said were collected from CIA director John Brennan's personal AOL account, the first in what the group said would be a series of publications.

Life-sized 3D-printed models of Chelsea Manning's face, created using her DNA sequencing, go on display at the World Economic Forum in Davos; Manning had been sentenced to 35 years in military prison for leaking state secrets to WikiLeaks.
A UN working group published a report finding that WikiLeaks founder Julian Assange is subject to arbitrary detention, a finding the UK and Swedish governments said they will not comply with.
WikiLeaks founder Julian Assange says he will leave the Ecuadorian embassy in London if a United Nations panel rules against his claim that he is being illegally detained.

Julian Assange is expected to demand that Sweden and the UK lift any threat of arrest so he can leave the Ecuadorian embassy in London, after a UN panel found his confinement amounted to arbitrary detention.
WikiLeaks representative Jacob Appelbaum says Julian Assange would find life no easier under a President Hillary Clinton, citing her office's reaction to the 2010 Cablegate leak.
WikiLeaks founder Julian Assange said his organization is preparing to publish more emails Hillary Clinton sent and received while US secretary of state.

Chelsea Manning, the army soldier who passed US state secrets to WikiLeaks, was taken to hospital and returned to barracks, and has been cut off from contact with her lawyers and all other outside connections for more than 36 hours.

Chelsea Manning, the US soldier who provided secret diplomatic cables to WikiLeaks, was hospitalized and remains under a doctor's care, her lawyer confirmed after days of the defense department withholding information.
Turkey blocked access to WikiLeaks after nearly 300,000 emails from President Erdoğan's ruling AKP party were published online.
WikiLeaks releases nearly 20,000 DNC emails, some embarrassing for Hillary Clinton due to revelations about DNC officials' views of Bernie Sanders.
Emails stolen from the Democratic National Committee were leaked via WikiLeaks, leading to the resignation of DNC chair Debbie Wasserman Schultz.
Sweden's court of appeal is set to debate whether to grant Julian Assange an open court hearing in his renewed campaign to rescind the arrest warrant against him.
WikiLeaks released hacked emails from members of the Clinton campaign containing excerpts from Hillary Clinton's paid speeches to top bankers.
Hillary Clinton's campaign accused WikiLeaks of being a "propaganda arm of the Russian government" after the site released a new tranche of hacked emails from campaign chairman John Podesta.
WikiLeaks publishes emails revealing that Blink-182 singer Tom DeLonge had contacted Hillary Clinton's campaign chairman John Podesta about UFOs and extraterrestrial life.
WikiLeaks released nearly 2,000 emails hacked from the Hillary Clinton campaign, allegedly by Russians.

Ecuador confirmed it temporarily restricted Julian Assange's internet access at its London embassy, citing WikiLeaks publications impacting the US election campaign, while the US and Ecuador denied conspiring to silence him.
Sean Hannity and David Duke praised WikiLeaks founder Julian Assange over the release of hacked emails from Hillary Clinton's presidential campaign.

WikiLeaks releases emails revealing blurred lines between the Clinton Foundation and the Clinton family's business interests, prompting the Trump campaign to demand release of all internal audit documents.
WikiLeaks-leaked emails revealed that Hillary Clinton's close aide Neera Tanden had called Clinton's use of a private email server "insane."

WikiLeaks released a new batch of emails from John Podesta's Gmail account, appearing to show Donna Brazile, interim DNC head, sharing a likely debate question with Hillary Clinton before a primary debate.
WikiLeaks is slowly releasing emails from the hacked account of Hillary Clinton's campaign chair John Podesta, which the article says provide a window into the Democratic party's elite.

WikiLeaks released tens of thousands of emails hacked from Clinton campaign chairman John Podesta's Gmail account, providing an unprecedented window on the inner workings of Hillary Clinton's presidential campaign.

Roger Stone said he was briefed in advance about WikiLeaks releases of Clinton-related emails through an American intermediary who he claimed had met Julian Assange, while Stone denied meeting Assange or having direct contact with WikiLeaks.
WikiLeaks founder Julian Assange was questioned at the Ecuadorean embassy in London by an Ecuadorean state attorney accompanied by a Swedish prosecutor over 2010 rape allegations.
WikiLeaks founder Julian Assange participated in a Reddit Ask Me Anything session, facing questions about WikiLeaks’ alleged links to Russia and whether he was still alive.

A lawyer for Julian Assange indicated that the WikiLeaks founder is ready to face extradition to the US after Barack Obama commuted Chelsea Manning's sentence, though the White House said the decision was not influenced by Assange's offer.
Ecuadorian presidential candidate Guillermo Lasso says he would give WikiLeaks founder Julian Assange 30 days' notice to leave the Ecuadorian embassy if elected.

Roger Stone wrote on social media that he had a “perfectly legal back channel” to Julian Assange, whose organization WikiLeaks published emails related to Hillary Clinton’s presidential campaign, then deleted the message.
WikiLeaks published thousands of leaked CIA documents detailing hacking tools, including techniques to compromise smart TVs and phones.
WikiLeaks revealed approximately 10,000 CIA documents in a leak dubbed "Vault 7," with the whistleblower's motives and identity remaining unknown.
US Attorney General Jeff Sessions says arresting WikiLeaks founder Julian Assange is a priority, and CNN reports authorities have prepared charges against him.
Chelsea Manning, who leaked a vast trove of US state secrets to WikiLeaks, is released from a military prison in Kansas after serving seven years of a 35-year sentence.

Swedish prosecutors discontinue their rape investigation into WikiLeaks founder Julian Assange and recall the European arrest warrant, though a UK arrest warrant for breaching bail conditions remains open.

WikiLeaks founder Julian Assange cancelled a planned press conference at the Ecuadorian embassy in London where he was to make a "special announcement," with his legal team saying he cancelled to allow negotiations with UK authorities to proceed.

A newly released Pentagon analysis concluded that Chelsea Manning's 2010 leak of hundreds of thousands of secret US documents to WikiLeaks had no strategic impact on US war efforts in Afghanistan and Iraq.
WikiLeaks founder Julian Assange claimed he contacted Donald Trump Jr. and urged him to publish emails via WikiLeaks, but Trump Jr. published them himself instead.
Julian Assange promises over a million WikiLeaks releases in 2013.
WikiLeaks is reportedly preparing to release a video of an air strike in Afghanistan, but no release date is specified.
WikiLeaks is reportedly preparing to release another video, this time of an air strike in Afghanistan against what the US government says were mostly insurgents.

facts.text: On 2010-04-05, WikiLeaks unveiled a graphic video of a 2007 US Army attack in Iraq that killed 12 people, including two Reuters employees.
On 2010-07-25, WikiLeaks disclosed more than 90,000 secret US military records about the Afghanistan war, one of the biggest leaks in US military history.
On 2010-10-22, WikiLeaks released almost 400,000 secret US army field reports from the Iraq war; Hillary Clinton and NATO condemned the disclosure as risking lives.
In 2010-11, WikiLeaks released a trove of US diplomatic cables; on 2010-11-28 it released 251,287 cables, the largest leak of diplomatic missives in history.
On 2010-12-08, WikiLeaks founder Julian Assange was remanded in custody in London pending extradition proceedings over sexual offence allegations made in Sweden.

On 2011-09-01, a security breach led to the unredacted WikiLeaks archive of 251,000 secret US diplomatic cables being made available online; WikiLeaks blamed the Guardian's book, which the Guardian denied.

On 2011-10-24, WikiLeaks announced it will suspend operations until the banking blockade by Visa, Mastercard, and PayPal is lifted, warning it lacks funds to continue into 2012 at current funding levels.
On 2012-06-19, WikiLeaks founder Julian Assange sought political asylum at the Ecuadorean embassy in London, sparking a legal crisis over his extradition case.

event-8757f56ca171077d.summary: WikiLeaks published more than 250,000 classified US embassy cables, revealing confidential diplomatic assessments of US allies and foes.

event-e394158a8a95d4fb.summary: WikiLeaks unveils a graphic video of a 2007 US Army attack in Iraq that left 12 people dead, including two Reuters employees.

event-adc1d0c0e7c91a16.summary: Chelsea Manning, the US army intelligence analyst who leaked a huge cache of state secrets to WikiLeaks, was arrested at Forward Operating Base Hammer outside Baghdad.

event-fd23ceba0205c56f.summary: US officials are searching for WikiLeaks founder Julian Assange in an attempt to pressure him not to publish thousands of confidential diplomatic cables.

event-b9e844ed51086be7.summary: WikiLeaks says it plans to release a secret military video of a deadly US air strike on the Afghan village of Garani in May 2009.

event-5786e53d37ee271b.summary: WikiLeaks founder Julian Assange is profiled as the driving force behind the site, which has published over a million confidential documents and faced more than 100 legal attacks since its 2007 launch.

event-559291e0f201efda.summary: WikiLeaks obtains and discloses more than 90,000 secret US military records about the Afghanistan war, one of the biggest leaks in US military history.

event-749b6595ca3eb557.summary: The White House implores WikiLeaks to stop posting secret Afghanistan war documents, saying the logs jeopardize national security.

event-10e9f83b6343c8e7.summary: WikiLeaks founder Julian Assange revealed the organization is preparing to publish around 15,000 withheld Afghanistan war logs after finishing checks, prompting condemnation from Reporters Without Borders and anger from the Pentagon.

event-d5e3a6ac86135a7f.summary: Michael Moore and Daniel Ellsberg launch an international campaign demanding the release of Bradley Manning, the US soldier charged with passing classified material to WikiLeaks, with demonstrations planned in the US, Canada, and Australia over the next three days.

event-41978d9b59c6143a.summary: WikiLeaks founder Julian Assange accused Wired magazine of having an agenda, not checking facts, and spreading misinformation about WikiLeaks, including a claim that the site was due to release as many as 500,000 classified US documents from the Iraq war.

event-b4c04596b9820651.summary: US Secretary of State Hillary Clinton and NATO condemned WikiLeaks' release of almost 400,000 secret US army field reports from the Iraq war, claiming the disclosure could put lives at risk.

event-bc4df782e95964e2.summary: WikiLeaks releases a second large trove of leaked US military material, the Iraq war logs, escalating tensions with Washington.

event-8ff43615b6c9d0ae.summary: WikiLeaks releases almost 400,000 secret US military field reports on the Iraq war, revealing previously undocumented civilian deaths and abuse, and Julian Assange speaks at a London press conference about the disclosure.

event-eecd968187c22d01.summary: The UK Ministry of Defence released details of 21 incidents in which British troops attacked Afghan civilians, incidents that were among thousands mentioned in US army logs posted by WikiLeaks in the summer.

event-438d5e21f48f1359.summary: WikiLeaks released a trove of U.S. diplomatic cables, sparking debate over secrecy and media coverage.

event-e1645f2db4023133.summary: WikiLeaks founder Julian Assange and his lawyer threatened to sue The Guardian over its plan to publish stories based on the US embassy cables, leading to a further delay in publication.

event-98c674bc23614309.summary: The UK government acknowledged it had been warned by US authorities about WikiLeaks’ expected publication of sensitive diplomatic files, with Washington braced for the release within days.

event-eeb713a7e3cee888.summary: World leaders were briefed by the US state department about expected WikiLeaks disclosures of thousands of sensitive diplomatic cables, and newspaper editors were asked to brief the government if they plan to publish sensitive diplomatic files.

event-b44cd12c42f9a5d6.summary: WikiLeaks released 251,287 secret US embassy cables, the largest leak of diplomatic missives in history, which were published by the Guardian and international partners.

event-1ea090ad8e2cc2f4.summary: The Guardian publishes the first in a series of reports based on more than 250,000 US embassy cables sent to WikiLeaks, with five publications having had prior access.

event-3aa5104b16fda2f5.summary: Interpol added WikiLeaks founder Julian Assange to its worldwide wanted list on sex-crime allegations, as the US announced an active criminal investigation into whether he violated its espionage laws.

event-206ee5ae96b64ed7.summary: WikiLeaks founder Julian Assange is scheduled to answer Guardian readers' questions live online at 1 pm, subject to his access to an internet connection.

event-9a65c55bce20a937.summary: The Guardian published a series of stories sourced from US embassy cables via WikiLeaks, revealing allegations including organized crime linked to the Russian government, China's growing impatience with North Korea, and alleged corruption in the Afghan government.

event-eff2fbd2e20c8d37.summary: Tableau Software removed its visualizations of the leaked US embassy cables from the internet after a public request from Senator Joe Lieberman, who called for organizations hosting WikiLeaks to terminate their relationship with the website.

event-217af23a695784e8.summary: WikiLeaks founder Julian Assange agreed to meet British police regarding a European arrest warrant from Sweden, while US Attorney General Eric Holder authorized significant actions toward prosecuting him over the release of diplomatic cables.

event-201b2f654cc98d8f.summary: WikiLeaks founder Julian Assange is expected to appear in a UK court after his lawyers said he would meet police regarding a European arrest warrant from Sweden over alleged sexual assaults.

event-4792367c475cd75b.summary: WikiLeaks says it will continue releasing leaked US embassy cables despite the arrest of founder Julian Assange in London on Swedish sexual offence allegations.

event-e4f3cfcf461d990d.summary: WikiLeaks founder Julian Assange is denied bail by a UK court due to his lack of community ties in the UK.

event-28c6ea270e5edd13.summary: WikiLeaks founder Julian Assange was remanded in custody in London pending extradition proceedings over sexual offence allegations made in Sweden.

event-37031a351fbac41b.summary: Lawyers for WikiLeaks editor-in-chief Julian Assange said they are preparing for a possible US indictment, though no charges have yet been lodged.

event-8ce1f6d91c28b028.summary: WikiLeaks founder Julian Assange, speaking from his Wandsworth prison cell, urges supporters to protect WikiLeaks from "instruments of US foreign policy."

event-8f33108a9757f09b.summary: The Crown Prosecution Service, not Swedish prosecutors, made the decision to oppose bail for WikiLeaks founder Julian Assange, who remains in Wandsworth prison.

event-cf48b95e768d6691.summary: Britain's high court granted bail to WikiLeaks founder Julian Assange, who is wanted in Sweden for questioning over allegations of rape.

event-31bee20e7ecb0b55.summary: Julian Assange said his life and the lives of his WikiLeaks colleagues are under threat, and Bank of America became the latest financial institution to refuse to handle payments for WikiLeaks.

event-66461dc6e6c3b592.summary: The Belarus-Telegraf state newspaper says WikiLeaks allowed the Belarusian dictatorship to identify organizers, instigators and rioters, including foreign ones, who protested against rigged elections.

event-a64a3a846cf5be32.summary: The CIA launches a taskforce named the WikiLeaks Task Force (WTF) to assess the impact of 250,000 leaked US diplomatic cables.

event-59eb1c88d86576dc.summary: The US State Department relocated a handful of foreign diplomatic sources identified in secret embassy cables released via WikiLeaks and warned hundreds of others about their safety.

event-0e12b58fb1aed928.summary: Julian Assange appeared in court for a procedural hearing on his extradition to Sweden and said WikiLeaks would continue its work unabated.

event-6d4b09b2f9e6a385.summary: Senior US State Department officials concluded in private briefings to Congress that the WikiLeaks controversy has caused little real and lasting damage to American diplomacy, contradicting the White House's public condemnation.

event-0eb7baa9641c0e2c.summary: A Guardian book reveals that WikiLeaks founder Julian Assange disguised himself as an old woman in a wig for fear he was being followed by US intelligence.

event-67c25bc8ed76b5bc.summary: WikiLeaks founder Julian Assange appears in court for a two-day hearing to resist extradition to Sweden.

event-a39e34e503bf7a73.summary: Julian Assange's lawyer made a graphic defence during an extradition hearing at Belmarsh magistrate's court in London, denying sexual assault allegations against the WikiLeaks founder.

event-f8cbe4b927dddcb4.summary: The Australian ambassador to Sweden wrote to Sweden’s justice minister seeking assurances that WikiLeaks founder Julian Assange would be treated justly under Swedish and international law if extradited there.

event-218395bc2bbe63d9.summary: WikiLeaks founder Julian Assange lost his extradition battle at Belmarsh magistrates court and is to be extradited to Sweden to face allegations of rape and sexual assault, though his legal team confirmed he will appeal.

event-a43e72312c7fcbc9.summary: Lawyers for WikiLeaks founder Julian Assange lodged papers to appeal his extradition from Britain to Sweden to face allegations of rape and sexual assault.

event-de077abd9299c876.summary: The Hindu newspaper began publishing reports based on US diplomatic cables obtained from WikiLeaks, covering Washington's relationship with New Delhi.

event-49d326fddff46fc5.summary: The Guardian was named newspaper of the year at the 2011 Press Awards for its partnership with WikiLeaks on the leaked US embassy cables.

event-0abbad5adbdb1078.summary: A leading British MP warned that President Barack Obama may have prejudiced the trial of US army private Bradley Manning, who is charged with leaking classified US documents to WikiLeaks, by saying at a fundraiser that Manning "broke the law".

event-dc6f9cd9aedb1747.summary: WikiLeaks founder Julian Assange appeared at the high court in London at the start of his latest fight against extradition to Sweden over sex allegations.

event-309994dc9798c43f.summary: A security breach led to the unredacted WikiLeaks archive of 251,000 secret US diplomatic cables being made available online, with WikiLeaks blaming the Guardian's book for the release and the Guardian denying the allegations.

event-81df42d563b591ed.summary: WikiLeaks published its full archive of 251,000 unredacted US diplomatic cables, potentially exposing named individuals to detention or harm, a move condemned by its five previous media partners.

event-bba95c6c343f4d05.summary: The Iraqi government announces a new investigation into a 2006 massacre of a family in Ishaqi after WikiLeaks released a diplomatic cable alleging US soldiers handcuffed and executed women and children and called in an air strike to destroy evidence.

event-1a4f276e51f19a19.summary: WikiLeaks announced it will suspend operations until the banking blockade by Visa, Mastercard, and PayPal is lifted, warning it lacks funds to continue into 2012 at current funding levels.

event-b3822b78a0124f62.summary: The high court dismissed Julian Assange's appeal against extradition to Sweden, narrowing the WikiLeaks founder's legal options.

event-955058720ed249a1.summary: WikiLeaks founder Julian Assange seeks to take his extradition fight to the UK supreme court by applying for a hearing to appeal against extradition to Sweden over sex crime allegations.

event-6dedb223f1fbe272.summary: A panel of seven UK supreme court justices is to hear Julian Assange's appeal against extradition to Sweden, with a two-day hearing scheduled to begin on 1 February.

event-f67b4f0f88ed3c12.summary: A forensic investigator testified that files on Bradley Manning's army computers exactly matched WikiLeaks-published US embassy cables and Guantánamo detainee reports.

event-4f67be32199b62aa.summary: WikiLeaks begins releasing a cache of what it says are 5.5 million emails obtained from the servers of the US-based intelligence gathering firm Stratfor, initially publishing 167 emails.

event-8737c5cc7e30e2cf.summary: A book chapter argues that mainstream media coverage of WikiLeaks' US diplomatic cables marginalized stories of significant public interest and delegitimized WikiLeaks.

event-ae7ec60c03e0f8a1.summary: Bradley Manning's lawyer files a motion stating the US government possesses 250,000 pages of documents relating to WikiLeaks and Manning but is refusing to disclose them to the defense.

event-6d1466697eb52bba.summary: WikiLeaks founder Julian Assange seeks political asylum at the Ecuadorean embassy in London, sparking a legal crisis over his extradition case.

event-81de4eaf28b266b1.summary: WikiLeaks founder Julian Assange sought political asylum at the Ecuadorean embassy in London after the UK Supreme Court rejected his appeal against extradition to Sweden.

event-8e2f7bb47754d85c.summary: Julian Assange seeks asylum at Ecuador’s London embassy, with his lawyer stating concern that Sweden might extradite him to the United States over WikiLeaks.

event-c2ad0e2b6a09ffcc.summary: A military judge ordered prosecutors to prepare a due diligence statement and hand over damage assessments related to WikiLeaks' publication of secret diplomatic cables and war logs in the Bradley Manning case.

event-3ad8e15f0e084314.summary: The US Department of Justice confirms that WikiLeaks remains the object of an ongoing criminal investigation.

event-a071b34701f83d98.summary: Baltasar Garzón will lead the legal team representing Julian Assange and WikiLeaks.

event-1f49a7b9de718d0f.summary: Ecuador’s foreign minister says Britain told Ecuador it believes officials can enter its London embassy and arrest WikiLeaks founder Julian Assange, and Ecuador says it will announce its decision on Assange’s asylum request on Thursday.

event-b299647f1d7b407f.summary: Ecuadorian officials say President Rafael Correa has agreed to grant WikiLeaks founder Julian Assange asylum, though Correa denies a decision has been made.

event-311a09fdacedad26.summary: Ecuador remains willing to negotiate with Britain over Julian Assange’s fate and proposes that the UK and Sweden undertake not to extradite him to a third country after the Swedish investigation.

event-8d83d2b9fc48afc3.summary: Ecuador's foreign minister says Ecuador received a written threat from the UK that it could arrest WikiLeaks founder Julian Assange at Ecuador's embassy in London, and Ecuador is considering his asylum request.

event-a4ea27266af80a00.summary: Ecuador grants political asylum to WikiLeaks founder Julian Assange, prompting a diplomatic row with the UK and Sweden.

event-c48e9f2b8526aa65.summary: Ecuador's president warns the UK that entering its London embassy to seize WikiLeaks founder Julian Assange would be an act of political suicide, amid a standoff over Ecuador's decision to grant him political asylum.

event-c9d2125013434391.summary: A police officer accidentally revealed a document showing plans to arrest WikiLeaks founder Julian Assange "under all circumstances" if he leaves the Ecuadorean embassy in London.

event-efb5819da2160cf9.summary: A military judge set the court-martial trial of WikiLeaks suspect Bradley Manning for February 2013, with Manning facing 22 counts related to leaking secret US documents to WikiLeaks.

event-966afba4b054470b.summary: Ofcom did not uphold Julian Assange's complaint that a More4 documentary about WikiLeaks was unfair and violated his privacy.

event-0c79ca93875bd21e.summary: WikiLeaks founder Julian Assange announces he will publish a new book, "Cypherpunks: Freedom and the Future of the Internet," on 26 November.

event-e0d365e7e865b95d.summary: A pre-trial hearing in the court-martial of WikiLeaks suspect Bradley Manning concluded, with the judge yet to rule on whether Manning's nine months of pre-trial confinement should reduce his sentence.

event-025ebd40a50a284a.summary: Julian Assange said WikiLeaks is preparing to publish 1 million new secret government documents as he marked six months of refuge in the Ecuadorean embassy in London.

event-a4ddc85ef8f4e175.summary: A military judge granted Bradley Manning a 112-day reduction in any eventual sentence for excessively harsh pre-trial detention in the WikiLeaks case, but declined to dismiss the charges.

event-d68da964b536c147.summary: A documentary about WikiLeaks, We Steal Secrets: The Story of WikiLeaks, premiered at the Sundance Film Festival.

event-7d99617f4f297bd4.summary: Julian Assange, speaking via videolink from the Ecuadorian embassy, attacks the upcoming WikiLeaks movie "The Fifth Estate," calling it "a lie upon lie" and "a massive propaganda attack on WikiLeaks."

event-84dc4f41af58527f.summary: Bradley Manning is expected to plead guilty to lesser charges, including wilfully communicating classified documents to WikiLeaks, while pleading not guilty to major charges such as aiding the enemy at his court martial hearing.

event-e5ed0bf78b229094.summary: Ecuadorean diplomats raise Julian Assange's case with the Labour party as part of attempts to resolve the diplomatic standoff over the WikiLeaks founder.

event-1d4ab906a7a3002b.summary: Icelandic MP Birgitta Jónsdóttir, part of the WikiLeaks team that produced the 2010 "Collateral Murder" video, arrives in the US to stage a New York exhibition of stills from the video marking its third anniversary and to protest the US government's clampdown on whistleblowers.

event-44cb6249394d0a3d.summary: WikiLeaks publishes over 1.7 million US diplomatic and intelligence records from 1973 to 1976 in a searchable collection called the Public Library of US Diplomacy (PlusD).

event-61da77d33edbcf66.summary: WikiLeaks releases over 1.7 million US diplomatic cables from Henry Kissinger's tenure as secretary of state (1973-1976), documents already released by the US National Archives and Records Administration, which WikiLeaks has made more accessible by converting them into searchable formats.

event-959bda2b0d22340b.summary: Supporters of accused WikiLeaks source Bradley Manning rallied outside Fort Meade ahead of his court martial, which was set to open on 2013-06-03.

event-6de481c44fbec258.summary: US prosecutors alleged in the Bradley Manning trial that Julian Assange and WikiLeaks had close ties with Manning, guiding his leaks and involving him in the editing process.

event-db81e8ab332e104d.summary: The trial of Bradley Manning, accused of leaking classified documents to WikiLeaks, opens at Fort Meade, Maryland, with legal experts warning it could set a dangerous precedent for free speech.

event-3aa093943766bddc.summary: Ecuador's foreign minister Ricardo Patino plans to visit London to meet Julian Assange at the Ecuadorian embassy, on the eve of the first anniversary of Assange's stay there.

event-ee5fb6bfee76dbaa.summary: Ecuador's foreign minister says WikiLeaks founder Julian Assange is prepared to spend another five years in the Ecuadorean embassy in London, as British and Ecuadorean legal experts agree to try to resolve the impasse.

event-af24eece1fae7f76.summary: Julian Assange said he will not leave Ecuador’s embassy even if Sweden drops its extradition bid, citing fear of a sealed US indictment and prosecution over WikiLeaks cable releases.

event-c9b9be1c94558dc2.summary: Defence lawyers for Bradley Manning, who leaked state secrets to WikiLeaks, filed motions calling for several charges against him to be dismissed, including the most serious charge of "aiding the enemy."

event-208cf275b427ffc8.summary: The first trailer for The Fifth Estate, a film about WikiLeaks and Julian Assange, is released online.

event-a31c78627393fb33.summary: The judge in Bradley Manning’s court martial declined to dismiss the “aiding the enemy” charge related to his leaking of state secrets posted by WikiLeaks.

event-b641b2492a57640a.summary: In closing arguments at Bradley Manning’s court-martial, the prosecution accuses Manning of transmitting hundreds of thousands of classified documents to WikiLeaks for notoriety and argues WikiLeaks was not a journalistic organization.

event-e195720cc2b5d1ac.summary: The WikiLeaks party unveils its candidates and abridged policy platform for the upcoming Australian federal Senate election, with Julian Assange appearing via Skype from the Ecuadorian embassy in London.

event-b2e2ad36ba22f0d9.summary: Bradley Manning, the source of the WikiLeaks disclosures, was convicted on most charges including seven Espionage Act counts but acquitted of the most serious charge of "aiding the enemy."

event-fc67019affea9309.summary: A military judge reduced Bradley Manning's maximum possible sentence for leaking state secrets to WikiLeaks from 136 years to a possible 90 years by merging several counts.

event-ca9e940cdbaa457d.summary: US government requests that Bradley Manning, who leaked classified documents to WikiLeaks, be sentenced to 60 years in prison.

event-ced7e65205739daa.summary: Chelsea Manning formally appeals to President Obama for a presidential pardon or commuted sentence for transmitting hundreds of thousands of state secrets to WikiLeaks.

event-7374a32489eaa63f.summary: Benedict Cumberbatch reveals Julian Assange sent him a 10-page email the day before filming began, urging him not to take part in The Fifth Estate, a film about WikiLeaks.

event-66b68f3ea1cd6146.summary: Ecuador's foreign minister accuses the British government of violating Julian Assange's human rights and says there is no UK will to find a diplomatic solution to his confinement in Ecuador's London embassy.

event-748ba6e0cb79bc2a.summary: Chelsea Manning says the military is continuing to deny her gender-reassignment treatment a year after she was sentenced to 35 years in prison for giving secret documents to WikiLeaks.

event-333630b44f6b8695.summary: Chelsea Manning, who was arrested for passing state secrets to WikiLeaks, breaks silence to criticize Obama's Isis strategy.

event-ad6ade19fe133c44.summary: Chelsea Manning, who leaked secret documents to WikiLeaks, sues the US military over denial of gender dysphoria treatment.

event-857a1d75a9b65ff2.summary: Google revealed to WikiLeaks that it had handed over emails and other digital data belonging to three WikiLeaks staffers to the US government under a secret search warrant.

event-15ed6bd893c9b740.summary: WikiLeaks released secret CIA files, including one on maintaining cover with fake IDs at foreign airports and a 2009 assessment of the CIA’s assassination program.

event-e6e7f8bf0210aac8.summary: The Justice Department obtained a secret 2012 warrant to seize the contents and metadata of three WikiLeaks staffers' personal Gmail accounts, which was kept secret from them for almost two and a half years.

event-5566fc1e3b544f7d.summary: WikiLeaks demands answers after Google handed staff emails and digital data to the US government.

event-4a949c1b70253b05.summary: A federal judge confirms that the US government is conducting an ongoing, long-term criminal investigation into WikiLeaks.

event-c253962c65916ed7.summary: Chelsea Manning, the US soldier imprisoned for leaking state secrets to WikiLeaks, joins Twitter with the handle @xychelsea, attracting over 1,000 followers before posting.

event-ba96204a21f3e056.summary: Chelsea Manning, serving 35 years in military prison for leaking state secrets to WikiLeaks, posted a handwritten letter on her new Twitter feed explaining that her tweets are dictated by phone to supporters, in a move to quash conspiracy theories claiming the feed is a fraud.

event-915d7e738f05c494.summary: The French government rejects Julian Assange's asylum request, stating he is not in immediate danger.

event-582b435efb079f92.summary: Sweden offers to negotiate an agreement with Ecuador to allow Swedish prosecutors to interview WikiLeaks founder Julian Assange in the Ecuadorian embassy in London, though the statute of limitations on some allegations is about to expire.

event-7283176d96991ee2.summary: Chelsea Manning was found guilty of possessing unapproved reading material by a Fort Leavenworth prison panel and sentenced to 21 days of recreational restrictions, avoiding solitary confinement; she was serving a 35-year sentence for leaking US state secrets to WikiLeaks.

event-cb23598db0b835f3.summary: Documents reportedly show Ecuadorian officials considered smuggling WikiLeaks editor-in-chief Julian Assange out of their London embassy in fancy dress or via other plots to evade police.

event-08093c58df56121b.summary: Scotland Yard calls off its 24-hour surveillance of the Ecuadorian embassy where WikiLeaks founder Julian Assange has been living, saying the operation is no longer proportionate, while stating that efforts to arrest him continue.

event-4fe5de4445a49717.summary: Ecuador requests that the UK grant WikiLeaks founder Julian Assange safe passage from its London embassy to a hospital for an MRI scan, which Britain declines while stating he can leave but faces arrest under a valid European arrest warrant.

event-42f1e626bca7ac19.summary: The Metropolitan police confirmed that WikiLeaks founder Julian Assange would be arrested if he left the Ecuadorian embassy in London to go to hospital for a medical examination.

event-638842e3e98f9d4e.summary: WikiLeaks released documents it said were collected from CIA director John Brennan's personal AOL account, the first in what the group said would be a series of publications.

event-40d171ae96fa054a.summary: Life-sized 3D-printed models of Chelsea Manning's face, created using her DNA sequencing, go on display at the World Economic Forum in Davos; Manning had been sentenced to 35 years in military prison for leaking state secrets to WikiLeaks.

event-016e00509c50cdba.summary: A UN working group published a report finding that WikiLeaks founder Julian Assange is subject to arbitrary detention, a finding the UK and Swedish governments said they will not comply with.

event-98582b80a8033241.summary: WikiLeaks founder Julian Assange says he will leave the Ecuadorian embassy in London if a United Nations panel rules against his claim that he is being illegally detained.

event-ec64a8e5a1a0cb58.summary: Julian Assange is expected to demand that Sweden and the UK lift any threat of arrest so he can leave the Ecuadorian embassy in London, after a UN panel found his confinement amounted to arbitrary detention.

event-b3042ebde01b5450.summary: WikiLeaks representative Jacob Appelbaum says Julian Assange would find life no easier under a President Hillary Clinton, citing her office's reaction to the 2010 Cablegate leak.

event-6a28ae190db50e89.summary: Chelsea Manning, the army soldier who passed US state secrets to WikiLeaks, was taken to hospital and returned to barracks, and has been cut off from contact with her lawyers and all other outside connections for more than 36 hours.

event-5501f51e0f55fae6.summary: Chelsea Manning, the US soldier who provided secret diplomatic cables to WikiLeaks, was hospitalized and remains under a doctor's care, her lawyer confirmed after days of the defense department withholding information.

event-3ee0c1df9135e96d.summary: Turkey blocked access to WikiLeaks after nearly 300,000 emails from President Erdoğan's ruling AKP party were published online.

event-31a10edd44c7e448.summary: WikiLeaks releases nearly 20,000 DNC emails, some embarrassing for Hillary Clinton due to revelations about DNC officials' views of Bernie Sanders.

event-b4b7865b69a8ae6a.summary: Emails stolen from the Democratic National Committee were leaked via WikiLeaks, leading to the resignation of DNC chair Debbie Wasserman Schultz.

event-339aa4e197141ca3.summary: Sweden's court of appeal is set to debate whether to grant Julian Assange an open court hearing in his renewed campaign to rescind the arrest warrant against him.

event-00020c6a73192581.summary: WikiLeaks released hacked emails from members of the Clinton campaign containing excerpts from Hillary Clinton's paid speeches to top bankers.

event-b881b61c2b70ad2d.summary: Hillary Clinton's campaign accused WikiLeaks of being a "propaganda arm of the Russian government" after the site released a new tranche of hacked emails from campaign chairman John Podesta.

event-e23cd0404e428c40.summary: WikiLeaks publishes emails revealing that Blink-182 singer Tom DeLonge had contacted Hillary Clinton's campaign chairman John Podesta about UFOs and extraterrestrial life.

event-9489563341c63ba9.summary: WikiLeaks released nearly 2,000 emails hacked from the Hillary Clinton campaign, allegedly by Russians.

event-6db8f5ebce900820.summary: Ecuador confirmed it temporarily restricted Julian Assange's internet access at its London embassy, citing WikiLeaks publications impacting the US election campaign, while the US and Ecuador denied conspiring to silence him.

event-9b2c22bc93b3107c.summary: Sean Hannity and David Duke praised WikiLeaks founder Julian Assange over the release of hacked emails from Hillary Clinton's presidential campaign.

event-22bc4cdd96f8424e.summary: WikiLeaks releases emails revealing blurred lines between the Clinton Foundation and the Clinton family's business interests, prompting the Trump campaign to demand release of all internal audit documents.

event-069062b0aaa1c1fb.summary: WikiLeaks-leaked emails revealed that Hillary Clinton's close aide Neera Tanden had called Clinton's use of a private email server "insane."

event-c0c06d0d497a5032.summary: WikiLeaks released a new batch of emails from John Podesta's Gmail account, appearing to show Donna Brazile, interim DNC head, sharing a likely debate question with Hillary Clinton before a primary debate.

event-cb56f2df3942e65e.summary: WikiLeaks is slowly releasing emails from the hacked account of Hillary Clinton's campaign chair John Podesta, which the article says provide a window into the Democratic party's elite.

event-080c69e4cefafb58.summary: WikiLeaks released tens of thousands of emails hacked from Clinton campaign chairman John Podesta's Gmail account, providing an unprecedented window on the inner workings of Hillary Clinton's presidential campaign.

event-36b22f0a3fd35176.summary: Roger Stone said he was briefed in advance about WikiLeaks releases of Clinton-related emails through an American intermediary who he claimed had met Julian Assange, while Stone denied meeting Assange or having direct contact with WikiLeaks.

event-d87253b557c23c22.summary: WikiLeaks founder Julian Assange was questioned at the Ecuadorean embassy in London by an Ecuadorean state attorney accompanied by a Swedish prosecutor over 2010 rape allegations.

event-5cdffb280c822225.summary: WikiLeaks founder Julian Assange participated in a Reddit Ask Me Anything session, facing questions about WikiLeaks’ alleged links to Russia and whether he was still alive.

event-d078c37bc091d023.summary: A lawyer for Julian Assange indicated that the WikiLeaks founder is ready to face extradition to the US after Barack Obama commuted Chelsea Manning's sentence, though the White House said the decision was not influenced by Assange's offer.

event-587c6666e83af634.summary: Ecuadorian presidential candidate Guillermo Lasso says he would give WikiLeaks founder Julian Assange 30 days' notice to leave the Ecuadorian embassy if elected.

event-81efa919dc6169ba.summary: Roger Stone wrote on social media that he had a “perfectly legal back channel” to Julian Assange, whose organization WikiLeaks published emails related to Hillary Clinton’s presidential campaign, then deleted the message.

event-a8b8a4e4ef25db07.summary: WikiLeaks published thousands of leaked CIA documents detailing hacking tools, including techniques to compromise smart TVs and phones.

event-5c5f141454a1fc84.summary: WikiLeaks revealed approximately 10,000 CIA documents in a leak dubbed "Vault 7," with the whistleblower's motives and identity remaining unknown.

event-ab4e7f68caf646d8.summary: US Attorney General Jeff Sessions says arresting WikiLeaks founder Julian Assange is a priority, and CNN reports authorities have prepared charges against him.

event-d5aa3f37acef61fd.summary: Chelsea Manning, who leaked a vast trove of US state secrets to WikiLeaks, is released from a military prison in Kansas after serving seven years of a 35-year sentence.

event-d25700e0f373a97e.summary: Swedish prosecutors discontinue their rape investigation into WikiLeaks founder Julian Assange and recall the European arrest warrant, though a UK arrest warrant for breaching bail conditions remains open.

event-5d741881d8dab67f.summary: WikiLeaks founder Julian Assange cancelled a planned press conference at the Ecuadorian embassy in London where he was to make a "special announcement," with his legal team saying he cancelled to allow negotiations with UK authorities to proceed.

event-14f5c2e8a41f2c61.summary: A newly released Pentagon analysis concluded that Chelsea Manning's 2010 leak of hundreds of thousands of secret US documents to WikiLeaks had no strategic impact on US war efforts in Afghanistan and Iraq.

event-5da5569f29395bde.summary: WikiLeaks founder Julian Assange claimed he contacted Donald Trump Jr. and urged him to publish emails via WikiLeaks, but Trump Jr. published them himself instead.

event-0c0106027385b9ed.summary: Julian Assange promises over a million WikiLeaks releases in 2013.

event-91e2ec42ef585a91.summary: WikiLeaks is reportedly preparing to release a video of an air strike in Afghanistan, but no release date is specified.

event-e9a61b97058a7661.summary: WikiLeaks is reportedly preparing to release another video, this time of an air strike in Afghanistan against what the US government says were mostly insurgents.

events.summary: WikiLeaks founder Julian Assange is profiled as the driving force behind the site, which has published over a million confidential documents and faced more than 100 legal attacks since its 2007 launch.
Julian Assange promises over a million WikiLeaks releases in 2013.
Julian Assange appeared in court for a procedural hearing on his extradition to Sweden and said WikiLeaks would continue its work unabated.
Principal photography begins on The Fifth Estate, a film about WikiLeaks founder Julian Assange, with Benedict Cumberbatch in the lead role.

The WikiLeaks party unveils its candidates and abridged policy platform for the upcoming Australian federal Senate election, with Julian Assange appearing via Skype from the Ecuadorian embassy in London.
A Guardian book reveals that WikiLeaks founder Julian Assange disguised himself as an old woman in a wig for fear he was being followed by US intelligence.
WikiLeaks founder Julian Assange is scheduled to answer Guardian readers' questions live online at 1 pm, subject to his access to an internet connection.

WikiLeaks founder Julian Assange agreed to meet British police regarding a European arrest warrant from Sweden, while US Attorney General Eric Holder authorized significant actions toward prosecuting him over the release of diplomatic cables.

WikiLeaks founder Julian Assange accused Wired magazine of having an agenda, not checking facts, and spreading misinformation about WikiLeaks, including a claim that the site was due to release as many as 500,000 classified US documents from the Iraq war.
Baltasar Garzón will lead the legal team representing Julian Assange and WikiLeaks.

Tableau Software removed its visualizations of the leaked US embassy cables from the internet after a public request from Senator Joe Lieberman, who called for organizations hosting WikiLeaks to terminate their relationship with the website.
WikiLeaks released a trove of U.S. diplomatic cables, sparking debate over secrecy and media coverage.

World leaders were briefed by the US state department about expected WikiLeaks disclosures of thousands of sensitive diplomatic cables, and newspaper editors were asked to brief the government if they plan to publish sensitive diplomatic files.
WikiLeaks releases a second large trove of leaked US military material, the Iraq war logs, escalating tensions with Washington.
The US State Department relocated a handful of foreign diplomatic sources identified in secret embassy cables released via WikiLeaks and warned hundreds of others about their safety.
WikiLeaks released 251,287 secret US embassy cables, the largest leak of diplomatic missives in history, which were published by the Guardian and international partners.

WikiLeaks releases over 1.7 million US diplomatic cables from Henry Kissinger's tenure as secretary of state (1973-1976), documents already released by the US National Archives and Records Administration, which WikiLeaks has made more accessible by converting them into searchable formats.

Senior US State Department officials concluded in private briefings to Congress that the WikiLeaks controversy has caused little real and lasting damage to American diplomacy, contradicting the White House's public condemnation.

A security breach led to the unredacted WikiLeaks archive of 251,000 secret US diplomatic cables being made available online, with WikiLeaks blaming the Guardian's book for the release and the Guardian denying the allegations.
WikiLeaks published its full archive of 251,000 unredacted US diplomatic cables, potentially exposing named individuals to detention or harm, a move condemned by its five previous media partners.

The Guardian published a series of stories sourced from US embassy cables via WikiLeaks, revealing allegations including organized crime linked to the Russian government, China's growing impatience with North Korea, and alleged corruption in the Afghan government.
The UK government acknowledged it had been warned by US authorities about WikiLeaks’ expected publication of sensitive diplomatic files, with Washington braced for the release within days.

WikiLeaks founder Julian Assange lost his extradition battle at Belmarsh magistrates court and is to be extradited to Sweden to face allegations of rape and sexual assault, though his legal team confirmed he will appeal.
A UK court ruled that WikiLeaks founder Julian Assange must be extradited to Sweden to face rape and sexual assault accusations, and Assange said he would appeal.
WikiLeaks founder Julian Assange appeared at the high court in London at the start of his latest fight against extradition to Sweden over sex allegations.
President George W. Bush appoints former Presidents George H.W. Bush and Bill Clinton to lead a joint appeal for emergency donations to victims of the Indian Ocean tsunami.

Interpol added WikiLeaks founder Julian Assange to its worldwide wanted list on sex-crime allegations, as the US announced an active criminal investigation into whether he violated its espionage laws.
Julian Assange's lawyer made a graphic defence during an extradition hearing at Belmarsh magistrate's court in London, denying sexual assault allegations against the WikiLeaks founder.

WikiLeaks founder Julian Assange is preparing to learn whether Sweden has been successful in its attempt to extradite him over allegations of rape and sexual assault, with a ruling due to be delivered at a London hearing.
WikiLeaks founder Julian Assange agreed to meet British police over Swedish sexual assault allegations, with his legal team preparing to fight extradition.

WikiLeaks founder Julian Assange refuses to comply with a Metropolitan Police request to surrender himself to a London police station, remaining in the Ecuadorean embassy while seeking political asylum.

A lawyer for Julian Assange indicated that the WikiLeaks founder is ready to face extradition to the US after Barack Obama commuted Chelsea Manning's sentence, though the White House said the decision was not influenced by Assange's offer.

Swedish prosecutors discontinue their rape investigation into WikiLeaks founder Julian Assange and recall the European arrest warrant, though a UK arrest warrant for breaching bail conditions remains open.

event.summary: The Guardian publishes the first in a series of reports based on more than 250,000 US embassy cables sent to WikiLeaks, with five publications having had prior access.
US Secretary of State Hillary Clinton and NATO condemned WikiLeaks' release of almost 400,000 secret US army field reports from the Iraq war, claiming the disclosure could put lives at risk.
A forensic investigator testified that files on Bradley Manning's army computers exactly matched WikiLeaks-published US embassy cables and Guantánamo detainee reports.

WikiLeaks founder Julian Assange revealed the organization is preparing to publish around 15,000 withheld Afghanistan war logs after finishing checks, prompting condemnation from Reporters Without Borders and anger from the Pentagon.

Ecuador’s foreign minister says Britain told Ecuador it believes officials can enter its London embassy and arrest WikiLeaks founder Julian Assange, and Ecuador says it will announce its decision on Assange’s asylum request on Thursday.
WikiLeaks obtains and discloses more than 90,000 secret US military records about the Afghanistan war, one of the biggest leaks in US military history.
The White House implores WikiLeaks to stop posting secret Afghanistan war documents, saying the logs jeopardize national security.

WikiLeaks releases a second large trove of leaked US military material, the Iraq war logs, escalating tensions with Washington.
A police officer accidentally revealed a document showing plans to arrest WikiLeaks founder Julian Assange "under all circumstances" if he leaves the Ecuadorean embassy in London.

On 2010-11-28, WikiLeaks released 251,287 secret US embassy cables, the largest leak of diplomatic missives in history, published by the Guardian and international partners.

On 2011-02-24, Julian Assange lost his extradition battle at Belmarsh magistrates court and is to be extradited to Sweden over rape and sexual assault allegations, though his legal team will appeal.
On 2012-06-19, WikiLeaks founder Julian Assange sought political asylum at the Ecuadorean embassy in London after the UK Supreme Court rejected his appeal against extradition to Sweden.
On 2012-08-16, Ecuador granted political asylum to WikiLeaks founder Julian Assange, prompting a diplomatic row with the UK and Sweden.

On 2013-07-30, Bradley Manning, the source of the WikiLeaks disclosures, was convicted on most charges including seven Espionage Act counts but acquitted of the most serious charge of "aiding the enemy."
